title: Tor bounds detected on pro-etale covers and open-closed decompositions
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $A$ a sheaf of commutative rings on its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For integers $c\leq d$, say that a complex has Tor amplitude in $[c,d]$ when its derived tensor with every module sheaf in degree zero has zero cohomology outside $[c,d]$; use K-flat derived tensor [def-pc-kflat-complex]. For a scheme morphism $f:Y\to X$ use the inverse-image ring $f^{-1}A$ and module inverse image [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. (i) If $\{V_i\to X\}$ is a pro-étale covering family and every $K|_{V_i}$ has Tor amplitude in the same interval $[c,d]$, then $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[c,d]$. (ii) If $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ is a closed immersion with complementary quasi-compact open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-weil-open-immersion], and $i^{-1}K,j^{-1}K$ have Tor amplitude in $[c,d]$, then $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[c,d]$. No quasi-coherence, Noetherian or finite-cover hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: For a scheme morphism f:Y→X use the specified proEtaleRingModulePullback with coefficient f⁻¹A and the identity coefficient isomorphism. The exactness instances in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] make its derived pullback precisely Mathlib mapDerivedCategory. The proved source-library mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso supplies the descent of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], and mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor identifies pullback of M[0] with pullback(M)[0]. No additional Kan-extension comparison is needed.

proof.text: Build the flat-complex tensor presentation from [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]: its chosen predicate on homotopy objects is exactly K-flatness with flat terms. Map the flat complex subcategory to this subcategory by the homotopy quotient. Whisker the total-tensor and derived-tensor comparisons and insert DerivedCategory.quotientCompQhIso on both the tensor output and its two inputs. This gives ProEtaleTensorModel for exactly siteDerivedTensorIndependentCoefficients. Apply proEtaleCanonicalTensorPullback, the existing pro-etale specialization of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], to the resulting two models. Its natural isomorphism and Step 1 identify pullback of H^q(K⊗ᴸM[0]) with H^q(pullback(K)⊗ᴸpullback(M)[0]).

For a cover fix M and q outside [c,d] and let F=H^q(K⊗ᴸM[0]). Step 2 and the local bound tested on pullback(M) give zero module pullbacks of F. Scalar extension along the identity coefficient isomorphism reflects zero: compare its tensor-extension adjunction with the inverse scalar-transport equivalence. The invertible abelian adjunct of the normalized module unit in [new-lem-weil-pbc-proetale-module-canonical-unit] then identifies underlying module inverse image with abelian inverse image. The abelian clause of [lem-sfb-proetale-object-inverse-image-restriction], with its unused constant parameter the lifted integer ring, identifies this with localization restriction. The quasi-compact cover hypothesis upgrades the weakly-etale precoverage cover to a proetalePrecoverage cover [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Apply the already proved source-library ProEtale.isIso_of_isIso_localizationRestriction, the pro-etale specialization of [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism], to the underlying abelian map F→0. Every restricted map is an isomorphism between zero objects. Hence the underlying sheaf is zero, and faithfulness of SheafOfModules.toSheaf reflects the identity-equals-zero criterion back to F. Vary M and q.

proof.text:
For (ii), fix any $A$-module sheaf $M$ and $q\notin[c,d]$ and again put $F=H^q(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M[0])$. Steps 1 and 2, first with $f=i$ and then with $f=j$, give
$$i^{-1}F\cong H^q((i^{-1}K)\otimes_{i^{-1}A}^{\mathbf L}(i^{-1}M)[0])=0,\qquad
j^{-1}F\cong H^q((j^{-1}K)\otimes_{j^{-1}A}^{\mathbf L}(j^{-1}M)[0])=0.$$
The equalities are exactly the two assumed Tor bounds, tested on the module sheaves $i^{-1}M$ and $j^{-1}M$. Now [lem-exc-open-closed-detection] applies to $F$ with $R_X=A$, $R_Z=i^{-1}A$, $R_U=j^{-1}A$ and the identity coefficient identifications. Its hypotheses are the given closed immersion and complementary quasi-compact open immersion; it allows an arbitrary sheaf of commutative rings. It gives $F=0$. Varying $M$ and $q$ proves (ii), with precisely the same interval $[c,d]$.
